message.content:
Fix several HIGH/MEDIUM security issues found in a production audit of the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon. Touch ONLY YOUR OWNED FILES.

## PRIMER
Next.js 15 route handlers + server actions. Rate limiter: `import { checkRateLimit } from "@/lib/rate-limit"` → `checkRateLimit(key, { max, windowMs })` returns `{ ok, retryAfterSec }`. Client IP: first hop of the `x-forwarded-for` header (nginx sets it). Auth: `import { currentUser, requireUser } from "@/lib/auth"`.

## FIXES (verify each before editing)

### A. `/api/log` — unauthenticated webhook-amplifier + request-blocking sink — `app/api/log/route.ts`
No auth/rate-limit; it AWAITs an outbound fetch to `NXEON_ERROR_WEBHOOK` embedding attacker-controlled strings, pinning a request slot 3s each and letting anyone forge "🚨 Nxeon" ops alerts. **Fix:** add `checkRateLimit(\`log:\${ip}\`, { max: 20, windowMs: 60_000 })` at the top (silently 204/no-op when over); the webhook fan-out in `lib/log.ts` is already best-effort but the ROUTE currently `await`s `logError` — make the route fire-and-forget (don't block the response on the webhook). Cap/keep the existing payload clipping. (Only edit `app/api/log/route.ts` — if `lib/log.ts` needs a change, REPORT it instead, it's not yours.)

### B. `/api/track` — unauthenticated unbounded row insertion — `app/api/track/route.ts`
No rate limit; every POST does `db.visit.create` (~1KB durable). **Fix:** `checkRateLimit(\`track:\${ip}\`, { max: 60, windowMs: 60_000 })` before the insert; over-limit → 204 no-op. Keep the existing bot filter + field clipping.

### C. Missing rate limits on auth-adjacent endpoints
Add `checkRateLimit` to: `app/api/domains/check/route.ts` (`domcheck:${ip}`, e.g. 30/min) and `app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts` (`console:${userId||ip}`, e.g. 10/min — this one already has an ownership check; keep it, add the throttle BEFORE minting the VNC ticket so a customer can't loop it into thousands of orphaned vncproxy procs).

### D. `/api/health` leaks internal error text — `app/api/health/route.ts` (and it reads from `lib/monitoring.ts` — do NOT edit that)
An unauthenticated caller can receive raw DB error strings (e.g. `password authentication failed for user "nxeon"`, internal host:port). **Fix:** in the ROUTE, map each component to a coarse public status (`operational|degraded|down`) and a GENERIC detail string; never pass through the raw `detail` from `getHealth()` to an unauthenticated response. If `getHealth()` only returns raw details, sanitize in the route before responding.

### E. 2FA enrolment silently disables existing 2FA + impersonation abuse — `lib/actions-2fa.ts`
`beginTotpEnrollment` unconditionally overwrites `totpSecret` and sets `totpEnabled=false`, even when 2FA is already on and with no re-auth. **Fix (within this file only, no schema change):** if `user.totpEnabled === true`, REFUSE (`{ error: "Disable your current 2FA first." }`) instead of wiping it. Also guard against impersonation: use the REAL acting user, not an impersonated target — `import { realUser } from "@/lib/auth"` and require `realUser()` to equal the user being enrolled (i.e. block enrolment while impersonating). Keep `confirmTotpEnrollment`/`disableTotp`/`verifyTotpForUser` working. (A `pendingTotpSecret` column would be ideal but needs schema — REPORT that as a follow-up; the refuse-when-enabled guard is the critical fix.)

### F. API token scopes never enforced — `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts` + `lib/api-auth.ts`
`authenticateApiToken` resolves `scopes` but the route never checks them. **Fix:** in `lib/api-auth.ts` add a helper `tokenHasScope(auth, scope)` (treat empty scopes as full-access for backward-compat, or `read` as the minimum — pick and document), and enforce a `read`/`servers:read` scope in `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts`. Keep the happy path working for existing tokens.

## OWNED FILES (edit ONLY these)
`app/api/log/route.ts`, `app/api/track/route.ts`, `app/api/domains/check/route.ts`, `app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts`, `app/api/health/route.ts`, `lib/actions-2fa.ts`, `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts`, `lib/api-auth.ts`.

## HARD RULES
Never touch schema, lib/rate-limit.ts (read-only), lib/auth.ts (read-only), lib/monitoring.ts, lib/log.ts, worker/**, or other files. No build/prisma/generate/restart/commit. No new deps. `"use server"` files export only async functions. Every change must keep existing legitimate callers working.

## REPORT
Per fix: file, what changed, the limit/scope chosen; anything requiring a non-owned file (list as INTEGRATION NEEDED, e.g. lib/log.ts blocking await, a `pendingTotpSecret` schema column, session-epoch revocation); risks.

Wait, there's a way to satisfy both: I can return the same shape with empty strings for `secret` and `otpauthUrl`, then add the `error` property. Since TypeScript allows extra properties on structural types when they come from function returns (not object literals), this would be assignable to the caller's expected type while still conveying the error information. The caller's `setEnrollment` expects a value assignable to `{secret:string;otpauthUrl:string}|null`, so if I return optional properties, TypeScript won't allow it—the required fields won't match. But if I keep `secret` and `otpauthUrl` as required strings and add an optional `error` field, the return type stays assignable and the caller compiles. So I'll return empty strings on error paths to satisfy the type contract while still preventing the database wipe, then surface the error separately. The empty-string approach with an error field is the safest option given I can't modify the caller — it prevents silently breaking 2FA while surfacing the error to the UI. The tradeoff is that returning an enrollment object with empty values will render the setup panel and leave the user stuck until they reload, but that's acceptable degraded UX compared to data loss. content.text:
All eight fixes are implemented. Here is the report.

## Summary of changes (owned files only)

**A. `app/api/log/route.ts`** — Added per-IP throttle `checkRateLimit(\`log:${ip}\`, { max: 20, windowMs: 60_000 })` at the top (first hop of `x-forwarded-for`); over-limit returns a silent `204`. Changed the `await logError(...)` to fire-and-forget (`void logError(...)`) so the response no longer blocks on the outbound webhook fetch in `lib/log.ts`. Existing payload clipping (80/500/80/200/2000) kept.

**B. `app/api/track/route.ts`** — Added `checkRateLimit(\`track:${clientIp(req)}\`, { max: 60, windowMs: 60_000 })` inside the existing try, before `db.visit.create`; over-limit returns `204` no-op. Reused the file's existing `clientIp` helper; bot filter and field clipping untouched.

**C. Rate limits on auth-adjacent endpoints:**
- `app/api/domains/check/route.ts` — `domcheck:${ip}` at 30/min (added a local `clientIp` helper). Over-limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`. Placed after the existing auth check, before the registrar fan-out.
- `app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts` — `console:${user.id || ip}` at 10/min, placed after auth but **before** the Proxmox `vncproxy` call so ticket minting (and orphan vncproxy procs) is capped. Over-limit returns `429` with `Retry-After`. Ownership check preserved.

**D. `app/api/health/route.ts`** — Added a `sanitize()` that maps each component to a coarse public status plus a fixed generic detail (`operational`/`degraded`/`unavailable`) via a constant table; the raw `detail` from `getHealth()` (which embeds DB error text/host:port) is never returned. The catch block now returns only `{ error: "health check failed" }` with no `detail`. Status codes (503 when db/proxmox down, else 200) and cache behavior unchanged. `lib/monitoring.ts` not touched.

**E. `lib/actions-2fa.ts`** — `beginTotpEnrollment` now: (1) refuses when `user.totpEnabled === true` (returns an error instead of wiping `totpSecret`/setting `totpEnabled=false`); (2) blocks enrolment while impersonating by requiring `realUser().id === requireUser().id`. `confirmTotpEnrollment`/`disableTotp`/`verifyTotpForUser`/`regenerateBackupCodes` untouched. No schema change.

**F. Token scopes:**
- `lib/api-auth.ts` — Added `tokenHasScope(auth, scope)`. Policy (documented in the doc comment): **empty scopes = full-access** (legacy tokens keep working); otherwise matches exact scope, `*`, resource wildcard (`servers:*`), or generic `read` for any `*:read`.
- `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts` — Enforces `servers:read` after auth; missing scope returns `403`. Happy path for existing/legacy tokens preserved.

## INTEGRATION NEEDED (non-owned files)
- **`lib/log.ts`** — The route is now fire-and-forget, but `logEvent` still `await`s the webhook `fetch` (3s timeout) internally. Since the route no longer awaits `logError`, the request is no longer blocked, but the server-side promise still holds an open fetch for up to 3s per event. Consider making the webhook fan-out truly detached inside `lib/log.ts` (don't `await` the fetch). Not a route-side blocker anymore.
- **`components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx`** (non-owned) — Its `useState` is typed `{ secret: string; otpauthUrl: string } | null` and does `setEnrollment(await beginTotpEnrollment())` without checking an error. To keep it compiling I made `beginTotpEnrollment` return required `secret`/`otpauthUrl` (empty strings on refusal) plus an optional `error`. **Follow-up:** update that component to read `enrollment.error` and show it (and re-show the "Set up 2FA" button) — otherwise the two refusal paths render an enrollment panel with an empty secret/QR and no visible message. The security guard (no silent 2FA wipe) is fully effective regardless.
- **Schema follow-up (E):** A `pendingTotpSecret` column would let enrolment stage a new secret without ever touching the active `totpSecret`, which is the ideal design. Requires a migration — out of scope here; the refuse-when-enabled guard is the critical mitigation.

## Risks / notes
- The rate limiter is in-memory per-process (documented in `lib/rate-limit.ts`); on a multi-instance deployment each instance limits independently. Acceptable for abuse mitigation, consistent with existing login throttling.
- `console:${user.id || ip}` — `user.id` is always truthy for an authenticated user, so this is effectively per-user (per spec). The IP fallback is dead-code-safe but harmless.
- Did not run build/tsc/prisma per hard rules; type-compatibility of the `beginTotpEnrollment` return with its caller was verified by reading the caller's `useState` type.
